answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can accept paid work, like a comet leaving a verifiable trail through a nebula of anonymous requests: the stake is slashed if peers prove fraud, while honest work slowly builds reputation that cannot be transferred. An attacker must therefore fund every fake identity separately and risk losing each glacier-slow deposit, so creating a thousand convincing fakes costs a thousand stakes plus the time to age them, which makes large-scale deception more expensive than the work it could steal.
